quotes.text: Plugins are for actions. Connectors are for knowledge. Most teams collapse that distinction early and spend the next year trying to recover from it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Condenses the core architectural decision of the episode into a memorable rule.

quotes.text: Policies govern behavior. Architecture governs what's structurally possible. A breach that flows through an ungoverned retrieval pipeline doesn't care how good your policy documentation is.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sharp argument that AI security is decided by architecture, not policy documents.

quotes.text: This isn't a copilot problem. It's a permissions problem that copilot makes visible at scale.

quotes.text: Copilot ROI isn't delivered by licensing the seats, it's delivered by what those seats can see.

chapters.title: What the Semantic Index Really Is
RAG Middleware and the Security Boundary

takeaways: Copilot hallucinates on business questions mainly because it cannot see line-of-business systems, so closing the grounding gap is an architecture decision, not a prompting problem.

Use graph connectors for knowledge and plugins for actions: indexed content inherits Microsoft 365 compliance controls and Entra ID ACLs, while custom RAG middleware adds latency and a parallel security perimeter.
Clean up source permissions, design business-readable schemas, migrate off the deprecated Graph Security connector and pilot with a small cohort before rolling connectors out tenant-wide.
hook: Copilot sounds confident but is often wrong because it never sees the systems where your real knowledge lives. This episode is for architects and Microsoft 365 admins planning or rescuing a Copilot rollout. You get a clear framework for choosing graph connectors, plugins or federated MCP connectors, plus a checklist to act on this week.
